Creates examples of the chosen species: audio, spectrogram and video

Source: R/examples.R
extract_examples.Rd

For each detection chosen with select_examples(), cuts the exact sound of the detection (BirdNET window of 3 s) with a margin of margin_s seconds before and after it, from the original recording (at its original sample rate). Saves in <output>/examples/<species>/:

  • the clip as WAV,

  • its spectrogram as PNG (see spectrogram_image()),

  • an MP4 video of the spectrogram with the audio (see spectrogram_video()),

Usage

extract_examples(
  am,
  species,
  n = 3,
  min_confidence = 0.85,
  no_doubts = TRUE,
  one_per_recording = TRUE,
  margin_s = 1,
  video = TRUE,
  style = c("cursor", "scroll"),
  fps = 25,
  window_s = 3,
  max_freq = 12000,
  db_range = 70,
  width = 1280,
  height = 720
)

Arguments

am

An audiomoth object with detections (analyze_birdnet()); the examples are saved in its results folder. A list of them extracts the examples of each recorder.

species

Names of the species: scientific or common names of BirdNET (case and accents do not matter) or IOC names. Also a named vector c("Cettia cetti" = 3, ...) with the number of examples of each species, as printed and returned by detected_species().

n

Largest number of examples per species: one value for all of them or one per species. Not used when species already has the number of each one. Species with n = 0 are skipped.

min_confidence

Minimum confidence of the examples.

no_doubts

Require that BirdNET proposed no other species in the same window.

one_per_recording

At most one example from each recording.

margin_s

Seconds of audio added before and after the detection.

video

Create the MP4 video (needs ffmpeg).

style

Style of the video: "cursor" (a line moves over the whole spectrogram) or "scroll" (the spectrogram scrolls under a fixed line).

fps, window_s, max_freq, db_range, width, height

Settings of the spectrogram and the video (see spectrogram_video()).

Value

Invisibly, the index of the examples created in this call (data frame with the paths of the files).

Details

and keeps an index, AudioMoth_<ID>_examples.csv, in <output>/examples/. Successive calls add their examples to the index (an example extracted again replaces the previous one). The paths of the index are relative to the examples/ folder, so the results folder can be moved.

Examples

# \donttest{
card <- system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")
am <- read_audiomoth(card, coordinates = "41.00, -3.00", output = tempfile())
#> 
#> ── AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Folder: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/AudiomothR/extdata/example/card
#> • Site of this card: AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 (41, -3; ±698 m; source:
#> argument)
#> • Map: <https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=41&mlon=-3#map=15/41/-3>
#> • Recordings: 16 in 2 days (2026-10-07 to 2026-10-15, Europe/Madrid time)
#> • Audio: 48,000 Hz, gain Medium, 0.7 min in total
#> • 10 with problems: duration < 3 s
#> • Battery: 4.9 V → 4.5 V
#> • Temperature: 11.7 to 34.4 °C
#> • Results in: /tmp/RtmpXUCCMs/file23378000f1b
am$detections <- read_detections(system.file("extdata", "example",
  "birdnet_detections.csv", package = "AudiomothR"))
extract_examples(am, "Cettia cetti", n = 1, min_confidence = 0.5, video = FALSE)
#> ✔ 1 example of 1 species in /tmp/RtmpXUCCMs/file23378000f1b/examples.
# }
